A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoLA/CoLA-M research. All pages, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original C4 pre-training results, GPT-2 activation measurements, nonlinearity ablations and GPU performance measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds longer-budget pre-training, BERT-large experiments and downstream GLUE evaluation.

M1.justification: Both versions use h' = B sigma(Ax) and the same CoLA-M checkpointing procedure. The auto-encoder terminology and application to BERT do not introduce a new algorithmic component or change the underlying construction.

E1.justification: v2 retains C4 language modeling and WikiText2 activation analysis, and adds Wikipedia pre-training with masked-token and next-sentence prediction plus eight GLUE tasks. This substantially broadens the represented data and task requirements.

E2.justification: Corresponding C4, scaling and system comparisons retain their comparator membership, including APOLLO in profiling. BERT/GLUE extends the existing CoLA-versus-full-rank comparison to another architecture. Newly discussed LoQT, CompAct and ESPACE are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 extends reported 7B training from 80k to 150k steps and adds a 350M experiment with 51B tokens, eight times the earlier budget. Its new BERT protocol uses 85B tokens, LAMB and a 128/512-token sequence schedule, followed by three-epoch GLUE fine-tuning with task-specific metrics.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds a targeted test of whether CoLA's advantage persists beyond compute-optimal training, comparing 350M models after 51B tokens. The original rank-scaling controls and nonlinearity-placement ablation remain, with the latter unchanged from v1 Table 11 to v2 Table 10.

E5.justification: v1 gives no seed counts or uncertainty estimates. v2 Table 8 specifies that GLUE metrics average the best five of ten random seeds. This adds selective aggregation and seed reporting for the new experiment; neither version supplies dispersion estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds 7B perplexities of 13.09 at 120k and 12.73 at 150k steps, beyond v1's 13.82 at 80k, and removes the 65k entry. Reported CoLA-M memory changes from 28.82 to 26.82 GB. New results include 350M perplexity of 13.96 versus 14.47 after 51B tokens and GLUE averages of 83.5 versus 82.7. These extend budgets or tasks, rather than establish same-setting gains. Figure 5 also revises memory bars.

T1.justification: v2 removes the explicit chain-rule gradient equations given in v1 Section 3.2, Equation 4. The effective-rank definition and compute/memory derivations in Appendices B–C otherwise remain unchanged apart from numbering.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the claimed experimental contribution from LLaMA to LLaMA plus BERT-large. The central efficiency contributions and headline claims of 2× reductions and 1.86× training throughput remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the earlier untested-architecture and overtraining limitations with interpretations supporting encoder/decoder and longer-budget applicability, while retaining industry-budget constraints and identifying MoE as future work. Section 3.2 adds explanations distinguishing CoLA from weight compression and width reduction. Some interpretations become overstated: uniform baseline superiority conflicts with Table 5's 350M perplexities of 18.95 for GaLore and 19.40 for CoLA.

D1.justification: New Appendix D.2 documents BERT ranks of 384 for attention and 512 for MLP layers, its optimizer, corpus and sequence-length schedule, and points to NVIDIA's training pipeline. The code footnote changes from a named GitHub repository to an anonymous repository. Existing LLaMA hyperparameters and profiling details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds LoQT and an Activation Compression discussion distinguishing CoLA from CompAct and ESPACE. It also adds BERT, GLUE and LAMB references and removes Sainath et al. (2013). The principal positioning against weight and gradient compression remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and method explanation are substantially rewritten around auto-encoders. Experiments are reorganized around training budgets, scaling is incorporated into Section 5.1, and training/inference profiling is combined. Conclusions and limitations are rewritten, and Appendices D and E gain subsection structures.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figures 5, 6 and 8, colors Table 1, adds the GLUE table and restructures the 7B table. It removes the separate checkpoint-summary table while retaining its values in prose, moves inference results to Appendix E.2, and resizes or relocates several other displays. These collectively substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly left non-LLaMA performance and substantial overtraining unresolved. v2's longer-budget LLaMA comparison and BERT pre-training with downstream GLUE evaluation directly address these important empirical gaps, substantially strengthening applicability evidence. Selective best-five-of-ten averaging without dispersion limits confidence, and the claimed seven GLUE wins actually comprise six wins and one tie. These reporting weaknesses temper, but do not outweigh, the broader controlled validation.
